title: Running away from home to New Orleans by freight train
summary: Frightened and nervous at school, he leaves New York around 1909, plays a bar piano in Baltimore, rides trains to Jackson, Tennessee and then New Orleans, and ends up in Storyville meeting Stale Bread.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was born a scared kid. My older sister used to pick up with a buggy, a boogeyman. I was so frightened I'd go to school. This is a true story. Byers watched two and two. Bingo. It's gone, see. I really went to the fifth grade. And I got so damn nervous. I told my father I want to go to work. Well, around 1919, they had avatars working at the 112th Street in Amsterdam, Avenue across the street from St. John's Cathedral. It's the second largest in the world. And all it had was one arch. It would take all day to get one of those big blocks up there. But they used to advertise streetcar rides to Philadelphia for a dollar and ten cents. That's right. It goes to Newark, Elizabeth, Trenton, and then to Philadelphia. So I left home. I'm telling the truth. I didn't tell my father nothing. Because I wanted to go out for myself. When I got to Philadelphia, I walked to Chester. And on come of Baltimore and Ohio railroad train. You go for two cents a mile them days. And I went to Baltimore. And I walked out towards Sparrow Point. And I heard the piano. And I was drinking Sash Brutal. So I went to the bar. A fellow named Sylvester Williams was playing. I said, I play. He got me a job next, that night. For one dollar. So that dollar, well, I had a couple dollars. So I took a streetcar ride. And the freight train blocks the train. So the train just dragged. And so I jumped out and climbed on them. And I went to Hagerstown. Hagerstown, I took another train and wound up in Louisville, Kentucky. I took another train and wound up, I don't know, something just told me, go. And I went to Jackson, Tennessee. And there's a moving picture where the train stopped. I went there. He said, I couldn't afford to pay a dollar a night. It was called Nicolette's, Nicololium's, Nic-5 cents for it, see. Got to have 20 people in there to make a buck. He says, where do you want to go? I said, I want to go to New Orleans. So he called a fellow outside. He says, here's the fellow who wants to go to New Orleans. He was a messenger. They had a car on it waiting to be picked up there. We're half a load of chickens and then half the car were eggs. The fellow took, let me go. So when he got to Jackson, he got to Carlton Avenue, he says, it's a good place to go to New Orleans. So instead of me not knowing the town, I walked all around the riverfront to Parker Street. Well, I had no place to go and I was kind of afraid. So I slept under a tarpaulin. They only had one shed then days. That's back in 1910 now. About about 1909. One shed on the, that was the Parker Street. So I got up in the morning, washed, I started walking. First thing I know, I was in Storyville. So I thought it was one of his, Alice, his Jenny on the doors and all that, the cribs and stuff, see. And there's a fellow, my name is George Spaffer, used to fix all the electricity for the cribs and everything else. And he's fixing with the piano. They had them days of things, the contraction turned down and had all the tin things on, and it sounded like a mandolin with the piano, see. So I got told him, he said, go around the corner of Pop Towers, Basin, Bienville Street. That's where the piano players used to hang out, they played for Little White, Josie Arlington, Dixie Shaver. So I met Mila Kuhn, they called him Stale Bread. So we started, he called it Buskin, so we used to go into Cadillac, Black Cat, San Suzie. They were different places, they had a piano. I played a little piano, he'd sing a song, I played a little piano. He'd sing a song and he'd pass the trade. We'd make fifteen, twenty, twenty-five cents. Now he got me a room at 708 Royal Street. They advertised, I'd see pictures doing carnival, with this fancy grill boy up the- The Okinaikon.
